articles.title: Patreon Income Tracker: A Monthly Reconciliation Guide
articles.description: Track actual Patreon gross revenue, fees, adjustments, and payouts month by month with a blank, privacy-conscious CSV and a clear reconciliation workflow.

opportunity.decision: The query already reaches the site, and the guide adds an actual-record workflow that the scenario calculator alone does not provide.

sources.title: Payouts Dashboard
claims: The Payouts Documents tab provides earnings, payout, transaction, refund, and tax CSV files.

sources.title: Earnings Insights
claims: The Earnings page is Patreon's record of gross and net income by month.
Patreon's public overview is a trend estimate and is not an accurate record for a specific month.

sources.title: Creator fees overview
claims: Platform, payment processing, currency conversion, taxes on creator fees, and payout transaction fees can affect creator proceeds.
A creator's applicable platform plan depends on the creator's own account history and settings.

sources.title: How to use your Relationship manager
claims: The Relationship Manager can export a filtered member CSV for membership-status reconciliation.

articles.title: UGC Rates: How to Scope and Price a Creator Project
articles.description: Build a defensible UGC quote from your own costs, deliverables, usage terms, and add-ons, with transparent math and primary-source disclosure and copyright guidance.

opportunity.decision: The UGC calculator already receives impressions for zero-click rate, pricing, and creator-income questions, while this guide adds a distinct scope-to-quote workflow and primary-source rights and disclosure guidance.

sources.title: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers
claims: A material connection between an endorser and a brand should be disclosed clearly with the endorsement.
A video endorsement disclosure should appear in the video rather than only in its description.

sources.title: Copyright Basics, Circular 1
claims: Copyright initially belongs to the author, subject to exceptions including qualifying works made for hire.
Owning a copy of a work does not itself transfer copyright ownership, and a copyright ownership transfer generally must be written and signed.

sources.title: Works Made for Hire, Circular 30
claims: Work-made-for-hire status depends on the employment relationship or specific conditions for certain commissioned works.
The classification affects who is treated as the author and initial copyright owner.
